title: Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.17053v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Structured Electronic Health Record (EHR) models typically represent clinical concepts as dataset-specific tokens, discarding their associated natural-language semantics. Consequently, relationships between concepts must largely be learned from EHR co-occurrence without directly exploiting pretrained linguistic knowledge. We investigate the contribution of pretrained language semantics to longitudinal EHR prediction through tEHR, a framework that converts clinical events into natural-language descriptions and adapts pretrained autoregressive language models through EHR-specific continued pretraining and task-specific discriminative fine-tuning. We evaluate tEHR across four MIMIC-IV prediction tasks, where Mistral-7B achieves the strongest overall performance against structured-data, code-based, and LLM-based baselines. Controlled ablations demonstrate the importance of lexical grounding, numerical values, and both adaptation stages.

translated_title: 评估用于结构化电子健康记录预测任务的预训练语言语义
translated_abstract: 结构化电子健康记录（EHR）模型通常将临床概念表示为特定于数据集的标记，从而丢弃了其相关的自然语言语义。因此，概念之间的关系在很大程度上只能从EHR共现中学习，而无法直接利用预训练的语言知识。我们通过tEHR框架研究预训练语言语义对纵向EHR预测的贡献，该框架将临床事件转换为自然语言描述，并通过EHR特定的持续预训练和任务特定的判别式微调来适配预训练自回归语言模型。我们在四个MIMIC-IV预测任务上对tEHR进行了评估，其中Mistral-7B相比结构化数据基线、基于代码的基线和基于大语言模型的基线取得了最强的整体性能。控制变量的消融实验证明了词汇基础、数值以及两个适配阶段的重要性。
tldr: 该论文提出tEHR框架，将临床事件转化为自然语言描述并通过持续预训练和判别式微调适配预训练语言模型，证明预训练语言语义能显著提升结构化EHR预测性能，其中Mistral-7B在四个MIMIC-IV任务上超越了各类基线方法。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes tEHR, a framework that converts clinical events into natural-language descriptions and adapts pretrained language models via EHR-specific continued pretraining and discriminative fine-tuning, demonstrating that pretrained language semantics significantly improve structured EHR prediction, with Mistral-7B outperforming various baselines across four MIMIC-IV tasks.
